A common complication of parenter- al nutrition is infection of the intravenous feeding catheter site,1-3 which can lead to septicaemia. Infection and colonisa- tion of central venous catheters may be reduced if the catheter is tunnelled through subcutaneous tissue before emerging through the skin.4 Strict aseptic techniques should be used1 for changing the dressing or bags containing the nutrient flu- ids. Misplacement of the catheter has been reported.3,5 Precip- itation of minerals, lipids, and medications can cause line oc- clusion.3 Thrombophlebitis can occur after the use of either peripheral or central veins.
